notes.C01: Strong idea for the dub job, but couples two tools through a cues contract and a calibration gate, so it is costly to build right and to keep in sync.
notes.C02: Directly attacks the 'reads like English' dub pace with free signals, but serves only the dub job.
notes.C03: Stops hidden ASR loops and misses from reaching fact-checks and summaries while shortening the card; the escalation budget is the only running cost.
notes.C04: Useful for fact-check, but a second ASR backend per token and a ledger block are justified only once real fact-check volume shows up, as it admits.
notes.C05: Fits the most common real input (captioned reels), gives a free Vietnamese judge and can skip the 3.3 GB MLX pass; the first test is clear.
notes.C06: Provenance is rarely asked for, and scraping originals and sound pages is a fragile, breaking dependency.
notes.C07: Answers the repeated 'link these talks with timestamps' job and cuts large token costs; an index that must stay in sync is the main upkeep.
notes.C08: Real token savings, but the rent ledger, leases and per-job renders add knobs and a second rendering path to maintain.
notes.C09: Right instinct (fix is unused), but many harvesters and monthly audits make a standing operational burden for one user.
notes.C10: Fixes a measured breakage (733 dead commands) and silent degradation, and deletes running cost rather than adding it.
notes.C11: Clever editor's view, but most of it adds card lines no measured owner question needs.
notes.C12: Tidy roster serving citing and casting at low cost; the value depends on multi-speaker media the owner seldom uses.
notes.C13: Cheap and well judged, but a small gain for the dub job alone.
